title: the outline check finds the same conflict every time it reads the same ticket
intention: The outline check returns the conflicts a ticket really has on every read, on every host: a ticket that contradicts an outline line is never cleared by one unlucky read.
why: Measured 2026-11-20: 784eb1e92866 (mark-and-clean, which contradicts outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2) was checked on Windows with conflicts [] (outline_checks/784eb1e92866-20261120T065349.json, Haiku) and went on to PROVED. Over the same outline on Linux, five of seven same-shape codemother tickets opened the 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 conflict and two (a2eaa93fa078, 0a1e6f1efe49) returned none. A check that clears a contradiction by chance is a hollow green, and the BUILDME lane leans on it.
traces_to: Law 8 (a hollow green is worse than a red: it gets leaned on); Law 3 (one read is n=1).
how: The check's reader is one Haiku call (MODEL, from rehearsal). The red-first proof cairn/devices/codemother/machines/outline_check/proofs/test_the_outline_check_finds_the_same_conflict_every_read.py runs check() N=3 times on Linux over a frozen copy of 784eb's ticket (cairn/devices/codemother/machines/outline_check/proofs/fixtures/784eb1e92866.ticket.json) and today's outline, expecting the 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 conflict on every read, plus a control ticket with no conflict. D1 finds the cheapest reader that passes, measured in this order: (a) the prompt names the clause-level contradiction test (by construction against filtering is a contradiction, not a distinction); (b) k reads with the union of conflicts; (c) a stronger model for the outline check alone. The first that holds at N=3 on both hosts is kept.

clauses.claim: on Linux, check() over cairn/devices/codemother/machines/outline_check/proofs/fixtures/784eb1e92866.ticket.json and today's outline returns a conflict on 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 on each of N=3 reads
the same proof run on Windows (akiendell) returns the conflict on each of N=3 reads
a control ticket with no outline contradiction (6cd13a3a5f42 frozen beside it) returns no conflict on each of N=3 reads
the outline_check proofs already in cairn/devices/codemother/machines/outline_check/proofs stay green

decisions.text: D1: the reader change, the first of (a) prompt, (b) k-read union, (c) stronger model that passes clauses 1-3. The build records which was kept and the reads it cost.
D2: a red-first proof, PROVES {1,3} on Linux and {2} on Windows, live reads (cost is about $0.17 a read, measured); fixtures frozen beside it.

out: cairn/machines/rehearsal (its MODEL is the rehearsal's; a change for the check is made in the check)

five same-shape tickets opened a 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 conflict on Linux; a2eaa93fa078 and 0a1e6f1efe49 opened none

per single read of 784eb1e92866 frozen: the old prompt named 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 on 2 of 5 reads exactly, 3 of 5 once the clause suffix '4.3.1.5.1.5.2(5)' resolves to its line; the clause-by-clause prompt on 4 of 5. The control 6cd13a3a5f42 frozen named no conflict on 6 of 6 single reads
measured.how: akienasus_cc_0 measure.py / runa.sh on akiendelllinux, live Haiku reader, n=5 per arm

measured.saw: union of 3 valid reads per check, two proof runs through bin/cairn test: 784eb named 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 in 6 of 6 checks; the control named nothing in 6 of 6. 'Every read' is a probability, not a guarantee: at the measured per-read hit rate p=0.8, a check misses only when all 3 reads miss, 0.2^3 = 0.008 (about 1 in 125) IF the reads are independent. HYPOTHESIS, not measured: the reads are independent. They share one prompt, one ticket and one model, so a miss may correlate. Falsifier: over a measured series, union checks miss the line more often than about 1 in 125, or the misses cluster (one check's three reads missing together more often than 0.2^3 predicts)
measured.how: tester runs test-775a49382325 and test-727111a0e28c on akiendelllinux at akienasus/0f44-same-conflict-every-read; arithmetic by akienasus_cc_0, asked by akiendelllinux_cc_orchestrator

measured.saw: cost of one proof run, for whoever reseals the outline_check component: 6 checks x up to 3 reads = 18 live Haiku reads, about 25 min wall (PROOF_TIMEOUT_S 1800). Measured: the 784eb half cost $0.67 and $0.76 (9 reads each, about $0.08 a read); the control half's cost is not printed. The earlier $3 per run was an estimate at $0.17 a read and is superseded: expect about $1.5 per run, and the same again per platform (clause 2 runs on akiendell)
